meta.problem: An agent that continuously scans for high-probability trade opportunities and drafts a trade idea (entry/stop/target) I can act on — learning from how its past calls played out, and eventually placing live orders through my broker. First test instrument: Deriv Volatility 75 Index (R_75), which trades 24/7.

agent.name: fx-trade-scout
agent.model_rationale: Newest Opus-class — the judgment call of 'is this genuinely high-probability?' deserves the strongest model. Each run costs cents; the scan can move to Sonnet later if cost matters more than edge.
agent.system_summary: Each run, fetches real R_75 (Deriv Volatility 75 Index) candles at 2 granularities from Deriv's public WebSocket API; reconciles open ideas in the memory store against what price did; scans for a high-probability setup on price structure/volatility; only on high conviction, drafts a trade idea (direction/entry/stop/target/R:R/invalidation/conviction) to /mnt/session/outputs/fx-brief.md and logs it. Draft-only — never places orders.
never_dos: Never place, modify, or cancel any order, and never call any order/trade/execution tool — this version is analysis and drafting only
Never fabricate, round-from-memory, or estimate a price/level; every number must come from this run's fetched Deriv data with its timestamp, or it isn't used
Never emit a trade idea without a stop and a stated invalidation; never widen a stop to manufacture a better R:R
Never present a setup as certain — always state conviction and what would invalidate it
Decision-support for the operator's own trading, not financial advice for third parties — the operator reviews and places any trade

outcome.description: Produce this run's trade-idea brief as fx-brief.md covering R_75 (Volatility 75 Index)
rubric_criteria: fx-brief.md exists and has a section for R_75 — either a trade idea or an explicit 'no high-probability setup' with watch levels
Every price or level cited is fetched from Deriv this run and tagged with its timestamp; no un-sourced or invented numbers
Any emitted trade idea states all of: direction, entry, stop, target, and the resulting risk:reward (>= 1.5:1)
Any emitted trade idea states a one-line invalidation condition and a conviction label (medium/high)
Prior open ideas from the memory store are reconciled first — each marked hit-target / stopped-out / still-open with the price evidence — before any new idea is proposed
No order is placed and nothing is sent to an external system — the output is a draft brief only

tools.notes: Order-placement tools are deliberately NOT enabled in v0. Market data comes from Deriv's public WebSocket API (app_id 1089, no credential) fetched by the agent via bash+python (websocket-client).

connections.notes: v0 data: Deriv public WebSocket (ticks_history candles for R_75) — no credential needed. v1 live orders: the operator's Deriv API token (own app_id + token) in a vault, behind an always_ask gate. Order tools stay off until v1.

stores.name: fx-trade-log
stores.purpose: Every idea (instrument, direction, entry/stop/target, timestamp, status) plus a running track record (count, hit rate, avg R). Read first each run so the agent grades its own past calls and adapts — the 'learn and improve' engine.

schedule.human: Hourly, 24/7 — R_75 is a synthetic index that never closes. ~24 runs/day. The agent no-ops (no idea) only if the data feed is unreachable.
schedule.kickoff: user.define_outcome (task + rubric above), with relative dates only

cases.name: case-01
cases.expected: Today's first verified run output, saved at close as the regression baseline

evals.notes: Trade setups are fresh data — golden answers age out. The Outcome rubric IS the per-run eval; the self-graded track record in fx-trade-log is the real-world eval that accrues. Case 1 = today's first verified output, saved as the regression baseline before promoting any new agent version.

defaults_applied.iteration_bound: Outcome stops after 3 grade-and-improve cycles per run
defaults_applied.write_actions: None in v0 — the agent drafts trade ideas; the operator places any trade. Live order placement is gated, in v1.

interface.how: Brief lands as fx-brief.md per run; reviewed in the terminal / Console. Run history + traces in the Console.

next_directions.why_deferred: Real money — earn trust on the track record first (recommendation, not a hard limit)
next_directions.how: Operator's own Deriv app_id + API token in a vault; agent places via Deriv's 'buy'/'proposal' API behind an always_ask permission gate + a stake cap; or a Deriv demo account variant first

next_directions.what: Add gold (XAU/USD) and EUR/USD back as instruments
next_directions.why_deferred: Parked while we prove the engine on R_75; they share the same analysis logic
next_directions.how: Add their data source (broker MCP connector or web quotes) and extend the scan + rubric to cover all instruments

next_directions.what: Real-time reaction instead of hourly polling
next_directions.why_deferred: Polling is the pragmatic v0; true real-time needs an event source
next_directions.how: Subscribe to Deriv tick stream and trigger POST /sessions or /deployments/<id>/run on a signal, or tighten the cron to a 15-min interval

next_directions.what: Backtest / strategy eval harness + networking lockdown + trade-log dashboard
next_directions.why_deferred: Tooling / hardening — not needed to launch
next_directions.how: Replay historical R_75 bars to score a new version before promoting; environment networking: limited + allowed_hosts (Deriv host only); a generated results UI over fx-trade-log + outcomes

next_directions.what: Re-run evals before promoting any new agent version to the deployment
next_directions.why_deferred: Process habit, not a build task
next_directions.how: Run evals/run-evals.sh against the new version; only update the deployment when verdicts hold
